forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Iran's President Pezeshkian stated at the SCO summit in Bishkek on September 1 that Iran would 'immediately reciprocate if the US returns to its commitments under the June MOU' — a conditional offer that per the forecast's ambiguity rule (conditional offers = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless US publicly accepts) resolves as NO. The US did not accept; CENTCOM struck three Iranian tankers on September 5. FM Araghchi stated on August 19 that 'Iran rejects ceasefire and demands a complete end to the war.' No unconditional Iranian official statement committing to mediated ceasefire negotiations was published before EOD September 6. Horizon passed without YES criteria met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The Israeli Knesset voted on 2026-07-17 to dissolve at the natural end of its four-year term — the first Knesset to complete a full term since 1988 (Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, July 17). The Netanyahu coalition maintained a one-seat majority (61/120) through dissolution; no Knesset roll-call vote confirmed a loss of majority below 61 seats. The dissolution was the Knesset's own end-of-term vote, not 'an early dissolution announced by Netanyahu.' Under both resolution criteria — majority loss AND early Netanyahu-announced dissolution — the outcome is NO. DA's OBE argument accepted: with Knesset dissolved and Netanyahu in caretaker status, the coalition-majority question is additionally OBE before October 27, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

indicators.name: Smotrich formally departs coalition
Degel HaTorah files formal dissolution motion in Knesset
indicators.expected_effect: Knesset dissolved naturally Jul 17; this path is closed

forecasts.question: Will Iran officially announce a formal maritime exclusion zone or equivalent no-transit zone covering part or all of the Strait of Hormuz before EOD 2026-09-11?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Day 2 of the 'within days' announcement window opened by SNSC Secretary Rezaei on September 7 (GlobalSecurity.org, IranWarLive Sep 7). No formal IRNA/Tasnim/PressTV communique declaring a restricted maritime area appeared through EOD September 9. NOTAM database showed no Iranian maritime restriction advisory as of September 9. The Tasnim-cited unnamed IRGC naval commander statement of September 7 described 'comprehensive maritime defensive measures' as preparation-in-progress, not a formal declaration. Judge accepts DA's partial reduction (-4pp from 0.62): the Oman corridor deal being in 'final stages' simultaneously (F6) creates a dual-track Iranian maritime policy — 'authorized' vessels via corridor, 'unauthorized' via enforcement — and signing the corridor first may slightly delay the formal exclusion zone declaration. However, the dual SNSC + IRGC sourcing for the 'within days' signal is more than standard announcement theater. p reduced from 0.62 to 0.58; 48h remain to horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IRNA, Tasnim, or Press TV publish an official Iranian government or IRGC communique declaring a formal maritime exclusion zone, restricted area, or no-transit zone in the Strait of Hormuz before EOD 2026-09-11. A military advisory or 'warning area' published via NOTAM or Iranian coast guard, carried by TIER1, also qualifies.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV (official Iranian state media) as primary, OR NOTAM database (NOTAMinfo/FAA), OR one TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing named Iranian official or official document.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: An informal or un-attributed 'warning' without official Iranian government attribution = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A threat of future declaration without an actual declaration = NO. A declaration announced but immediately rescinded before EOD Sep 11 = NO.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and Oman issue a formal joint or parallel public statement establishing a Hormuz transit corridor, with explicit reference to IMO notification, before EOD 2026-09-11?

Oman FM Albusaidi had not published a parallel or joint statement as of September 9. No IMO circular for a Hormuz corridor appeared. IRGC attacks on commercial vessels on September 5-6 — on what Iran characterized as the 'unauthorized route' — are not necessarily contradictory to a corridor covering 'authorized' vessels, but they complicate Oman's domestic political position on signing publicly before enforcement ceases. DA hygiene: all criteria pass. 48h remain to horizon. DA opposing narrative addressed separately.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iranian and Omani foreign ministries both — jointly or in parallel — publish formal statements establishing a transit corridor arrangement and stating they are notifying or have notified the IMO, before EOD 2026-09-11.
